title: The Teacher Who Stayed
paragraphs: Ketika sekolah di kota kecilnya menghadapi penutupan karena menurunnya pendaftaran dan pemotongan dana, Widya ditawari posisi bergaji tinggi di sebuah akademi swasta bergengsi di ibu kota. Hampir setiap rekan kerja yang menerima tawaran serupa menerimanya tanpa ragu, dengan alasan bahwa sekolah yang berjuang dan kekurangan dana tidak lagi pantas dikorbankan demi karier yang nyaman dan aman. Widya, bagaimanapun, tetap tinggal, berargumen bahwa murid-murid yang tersisa, banyak dari keluarga dengan sedikit pilihan pendidikan lain, membutuhkan kesinambungan dan stabilitas selama masa transisi yang sudah sulit bagi sekolah itu.

Selama tiga tahun, ia bekerja dengan gaji yang sangat berkurang dan bahan ajar yang usang, sering membeli perlengkapan dasar dari kantongnya sendiri agar kelas-kelas penting tetap berjalan lancar untuk murid-muridnya. Perlahan, melalui pengajuan hibah yang gigih dan upaya penggalangan dana komunitas, sekolah itu secara bertahap stabil, akhirnya mendapatkan cukup dana untuk tetap terbuka secara permanen bagi komunitas sekitar. Melihat kembali, Widya berkata ia tidak pernah memandang pilihannya sebagai pengorbanan, karena menyaksikan murid-muridnya berhasil meski dalam kesulitan nyata memberinya rasa tujuan yang tidak dapat digantikan gaji yang lebih tinggi mana pun.
answerKey: When the school in her small town faced closure due to declining enrollment and funding cuts, Widya was offered a well-paying position at a prestigious private academy in the capital city. Nearly every colleague who received similar offers accepted them without hesitation, reasoning that a struggling, underfunded school was not worth sacrificing a comfortable, secure career for much longer. Widya, however, remained, arguing that the remaining students, many from families with few other educational options, needed continuity and stability during an already difficult transition period for the school. For three years, she worked with a significantly reduced salary and outdated materials, often purchasing basic supplies from her own pocket to keep essential classes running smoothly for her students. Slowly, through persistent grant applications and community fundraising efforts, the school gradually stabilized, eventually securing enough funding to remain permanently open for the surrounding community. Looking back, Widya says she never viewed her choice as a sacrifice, since watching her students succeed despite genuine hardship gave her a sense of purpose no higher salary could have replaced.
